answer: A practical defence is a refundable stake tied to each identity: an agent must lock a deposit before it can claim rewards, and peers slash that deposit if the same identity submits duplicate or contradictory work. Like a quill signing a ledger, each claim is bound to one stake, so creating many fake identities multiplies the locked capital rather than multiplying influence. A plume of cheap copies yields no nectar, because rewards flow only after independent peers attest the work and the stake survives a challenge window.
